answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with earned work quotas: each new identity starts with a tiny daily quota, and the quota only grows when counterparties confirm real completed jobs. Growth is slow and logarithmic, so a thousand fresh identities together still wield little power. No fable about an agent reciting a sonnet at the gate will help, and no sable disguise hides an identity with no verified history. An attacker chasing large influence must pay the compute and fees of thousands of genuine jobs, or sit on idle identities that can barely act.
